hints: Look at each list and spot the odd one out. Which two structures in the options are made only of membranes or microtubules with no DNA or RNA of their own?
Remember the three places with their own DNA in a plant cell, plus where RNA is found free and as part of ribosomes.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as a nucleic acid**

Great start. Nucleic acids means DNA and RNA. So we are looking for structures that contain DNA, RNA, or both.

Remember: DNA is not only in the nucleus.

**Pick out the structures with their own DNA**

In eukaryotes, three structures have DNA. The nucleus has linear chromosomal DNA. Mitochondria and chloroplasts both have small circular DNA plus their own RNA for making some proteins.

So any correct answer can include nuclei, mitochondria and chloroplasts.

**Add the structures with RNA**

Ribosomes are made of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) plus protein, so they definitely count. The cytoplasm also counts because it contains messenger RNA (mRNA) and transfer RNA (tRNA) moving between nucleus and ribosomes.

**Eliminate the structures with no nucleic acid**

Centrioles are made of microtubules, which is tubulin protein only. Golgi bodies are membrane sacs for modification and packaging, with no DNA or RNA. Any option containing either of these must be wrong, which leaves only option D.

options.A: Golgi bodies have no DNA or RNA, they are just membranes for processing proteins, so this list fails even though the other three do contain nucleic acids.
options.B: Centrioles are made only of tubulin protein microtubules with no nucleic acid, so this list fails even though the other three are correct.
options.C: Again centrioles spoil this list because they contain no DNA or RNA, even though mitochondria, nuclei and ribosomes all do.
options.D: All four contain nucleic acids: chloroplasts and mitochondria have their own DNA and RNA, ribosomes contain rRNA, and cytoplasm contains mRNA and tRNA.
